sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.697 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 328, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Faizabad/ Ayodhya.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant in the year 2022.
Subsequently, the entire matrimonial family had used to harass her and ultimately she was killed on 16.10.2023.
As per the postmortem report, the cause of death could not be ascertained and hence, the viscera was preserved.

sentences.text: 4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the postmortem report, which does not indicate any injury and the fact that there is no specific statement against the applicant to suggest that soon before her death, the victim was subjected to any physical or mental harassment in relation to any demand of dowry coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 25.02.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Rahul Chauhan @ Rahul be released on bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
